body:
_Original comment by_ **Jason R. Coombs (BitBucket: [jaraco](http://bitbucket.org/jaraco), GitHub: [jaraco](http://github.com/jaraco))**:

---

The test that elicited this error has been around for a long time in the [irc](/jaraco/irc) library. I'm pretty sure the test worked at one time, but I even rolled back to pytest 2.5.2, and it still failed (though more silently). I suspect the issue lies in py.

_Original comment by_ **Jason R. Coombs (BitBucket: [jaraco](http://bitbucket.org/jaraco), GitHub: [jaraco](http://github.com/jaraco))**:

---

Aha! The error only occurs when the doctest fails. If the doctest is passing, the error doesn't occur.

I don't think it is related. 710 is about comparing matching and non-matching results and this issue is when a Unicode character not in the file system encoding (or maybe another encoding) appears in a failing doctest. I haven't tried this on a non-Windows system, so I'll do that now to see if it behaves differently or if I can identify which encoding is relevant.

On OS X, the test fails as expected:

```
$ py.test test.py --doctest-modules
====================================== test session starts =======================================
platform darwin -- Python 3.4.3 -- py-1.4.30 -- pytest-2.7.2
rootdir: /Users/jaraco/Dropbox/code/public/pytest, inifile: tox.ini
collected 1 items 

test.py F

============================================ FAILURES ============================================
_______________________________________ [doctest] test.foo _______________________________________
002     """
003     >>> name = 'с'
Expected:
    'anything'
Got nothing

/Users/jaraco/Dropbox/code/public/pytest/issue628/test.py:3: DocTestFailure
==================================== 1 failed in 0.08 seconds ====================================
```

On that system, getfilesystemencoding returns 'utf-8'.

The following standalone Python script will replicate the error message when run on Windows or any other system where `locale.getpreferredencoding(False) == 'cp-1252'` (ref [open docs](https://docs.python.org/3.4/library/functions.html#open)):

```
some_unicode = 'с'

with open('file.txt', 'wb') as binary_file:
    binary_file.write(some_unicode.encode('utf-8'))

with open('file.txt', 'r') as text_file:
    result = text_file.read()

assert some_unicode == result
```

It seems the issue is that something in the doctest runner is saving the output to a file using UTF-8 encoding, but then when it attempts to read that file, it defaults to `locale.getpreferredencoding`. The patch applied in my fork (referenced above) corrects the issue (though I suspect it may not work on Python 2 and probably deserves more review).
@jaraco should one of us pick it up, I have @nicoddemus in mind
@RonnyPfannschmidt Yes, please - if possible. I don't have any actions or ideas pending beyond what I've mentioned above.

issue.title: Fix decode error in Python 2.7 when docstrings contain a non-ascii character

repository.name: pytest
repository.description: The pytest framework makes it easy to write small tests, yet scales to support complex functional testing

issue.body:
My initial approach to fix this was to correct how we were opening the file:

``` diff
--- a/_pytest/doctest.py
+++ b/_pytest/doctest.py
@@ -81,7 +81,9 @@ class DoctestItem(pytest.Item):
             reprlocation = ReprFileLocation(filename, lineno, message)
             checker = _get_unicode_checker()
             REPORT_UDIFF = doctest.REPORT_UDIFF
-            filelines = py.path.local(filename).readlines(cr=0)
+            import io
+            with io.open(str(filename), 'rU', encoding='UTF-8') as f:
+                filelines = [x.rstrip('\n') for x in f.readlines()]
             lines = []
             if lineno is not None:
                 i = max(test.lineno, max(0, lineno - 10)) # XXX?
```

But assuming that the file was in `utf-8` let me uneasy.

Studying the code a little more I realized that the `DocTest` object already contained the docstring that resulted in the failure, so there was no need to open the source to obtain it.

I also added a test to ensure that I was getting the exact same failure representation from the previous code, which shows some context lines before the offending line.

I would appreciate if @jaraco could test this branch on his test suites with doctests to ensure I didn't miss anything.

Fix #628
